Android lets FaunaLapse switch the screen off only if you allow it once, on the next screen. FaunaLapse then becomes a "device admin app" with one right only: to lock the screen (Screen off button, or by itself after the set minutes). The session goes on.

Some phones then show a red warning with a general list of rights (such as erase all data): FaunaLapse uses only the screen lock, as Android's page before it shows.

Remove this right before you uninstall FaunaLapse (under Last session, battery and clock).

Without it: press the power button gently, so the phone does not move, or wait for the phone's screen timeout.

Pack photo sessions for the computer

Pack puts each finished photo session into one zip file, next to its folder: a computer copies it up to 9 times faster than thousands of photos (over a USB cable). The photos are not compressed, so it is quick: 1 to 2 minutes for 5000 photos of 1280 px, up to 1.5 minutes per GB for larger photos (slowest on memory cards). Best with the phone on the charger. Packing goes on with the screen off (a notification shows it); if Android stops it, tap Pack again: nothing is lost. FaunaLapse checks every file in the zip, then deletes the session folder. On the computer, extract the zip (Windows: right click, Extract All) to get the folder back. Sessions over 4 GB or 65000 files, or packed with little free space, get more zips (_part2 and on): extract them all into one folder. Video sessions are not packed (few large files copy fast).

• Set up by, habitat, camera height and distance to target are named as in Camtrap DP (a data standard for camera traps), so the records can be shared in it.
• Plant: or what else you observe. Sample ID: for other targets. Session ID: your own name for a recording plan, the same for all its sessions.
• Distance to target: where the phone tells the lens distance, the fixed focus fills it in. Type a measured value to replace it; empty the field to get the focus distance back.

Where the phone stands, saved in each session\'s record.\n• Get location: use it under open sky. Without network the first position can take a few minutes.\n• Or type the position from another GPS device. Empty latitude, longitude and uncertainty to remove it.
Coordinate system: WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), decimal degrees (as on GPS devices and web maps), also for typed values.

Part of the position: how far the true position may be from these coordinates. Android\'s GPS gives a radius with a 68 % chance of holding the true position (Camtrap DP: coordinateUncertainty). A typed value should come from the device that measured the position.

Only for Get location: the search stops as soon as the uncertainty is this small or smaller, and the GPS goes off; otherwise it stops after 3 min with the best position. A smaller value can take longer; 0 m always takes the full 3 min. It is not the uncertainty of the position (the field above); the record keeps both.
Phones often cannot reach an uncertainty under %1$d m: the search may then run the full %2$d min.
0 m: the search always runs the full %1$d min.
Stop at: use a whole number from 0 to %1$d m.
No position: tap Get location, or type it from another GPS device.

Time between photos in a burst. Default 2 s: a 3 s step caught about 90 % of insect visits (Edwards et al. 2015).
Default 60 s: longer than a typical visit (about 11 s).

Photos and video: the square is shrunk to this size when saved. A multiple of 32 from 224 to 4096 (detectors and video encoders work in blocks of 16 or 32 pixels). Default 1280 px: the input size of many insect detectors. A square with fewer real pixels is never enlarged: it is saved at its own size, rounded down to a multiple of 32 (the aim screen shows both). Old phones may save video smaller if their hardware cannot take the size.
One video file per clip. Default 5 min.
Default 5: enough to follow insects from frame to frame on a computer. Use 10 or 15 for fast insects. On a test phone, 5 frames per s used about 55 % of the storage of 15, and 10 about 80 %.
Default 5 min: the camera rests about 83 % of the time with 60 s bursts, half with 5 min clips. It is switched off in breaks over 30 s. 0 = no break.
Default 1 h, a usual observation period. At most 720 h (30 days), day and night.
Clock times, for example 06:00-08:00, 17:00-20:00. 22:00-04:00 crosses midnight; 00:00-24:00 records all day. Default 05:00-21:00: early morning and evening visits count (Toivonen and Humberg 2026).
Default 1. Counted from the first window not yet over: a phone started in the evening begins the next morning. For more days, use a power supply.

35 to 50 °C. Default 45 °C: phones still work, but most stop charging near 45 °C and the battery wears fast above it. The pause lasts until the battery is 3 °C cooler. The session also stops cleanly at 15 % without charging, or when the storage is nearly full.

During a session, if you forget Screen off: the screen goes off this many minutes after the last touch (a screen left on uses energy and warms the phone). 1 to 10 min, 0 = never. Default 3 min: time to see the first photos. Not while the session is paused by hand. Needs the Screen off right (the first tap on Screen off asks). The power button wakes the screen.
Screen off is not allowed yet (the first tap on Screen off during a session asks): until then the phone\'s own screen timeout switches the screen off (now %1$s).
Never: the screen goes off with Screen off, the power button or the phone\'s own screen timeout (now %1$s).

A phone used only as a camera

Such a phone saves energy and is less likely to stop the app:
• Reset it to factory settings; no Google account, no SIM card.
• Turn off automatic app and system updates.
• Uninstall or disable the apps you do not need (Settings, Apps).
• Set the exact time, then turn on airplane mode (flight mode): without network the clock is not corrected, and file names and the session record use it.
• Some phones stop apps with their own battery manager. Huawei: allow FaunaLapse by hand to start and run in the background (Battery, App launch). Xiaomi: set battery saver to No restrictions. Samsung: add FaunaLapse to Never sleeping apps.
• Before the field day, test a session with the screen off.
After Start, tap Screen off on the status card (or press the power button gently): the session goes on with the screen off.

For the developers, only in this test build: these tests measure what the back camera of a phone model can do, so FaunaLapse can be made to work well on it. Sessions do not need them.

One test photo: checks that the camera works with the screen off. It opens the camera with the older camera interface, waits 5 s for the exposure, focuses once, takes one full photo and closes.

Speed test (about 3 minutes): how fast full photos can follow each other (both camera interfaces, 4 photo sizes), how fast preview frames can be saved, and which video sizes and frame rates record. On a computer, tools/phase0_speed_report.py sums up the results.
